name: Frame Interpolation and Restoration
title: Frame Interpolation and Restoration
answer: Frame interpolation and restoration covers the work of repairing and smoothing moving images: removing dirt, scratches, noise and compression artefacts from old or damaged footage, and generating new frames between existing ones so that material shot at a low frame rate plays back smoothly. It sits inside cinematography and video synthesis because the same models that invent plausible intermediate frames are also used to reconstruct missing or degraded ones. The field spans archive and broadcast restoration, streaming and display processing, and post production finishing, and it is distinct from upscaling, which changes resolution rather than timing or damage.

sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on GPUs, usually in the cloud for archive jobs and on workstations for finishing, with the heavy lifting done by optical flow estimators and video diffusion or transformer models. Restoration pipelines typically combine a flow network with a synthesis network, while interpolation models such as RIFE and FILM are common in real time playback and editing tools. Storage and bandwidth matter as much as compute, because restoration is often applied to full length reels at high resolution, and the site tracks 1,000 video models alongside the image and audio model counts, which reflects how crowded this layer has become.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Practitioners start by stabilising and cleaning the source, then estimate motion between neighbouring frames and use that motion to warp or synthesise the frame that should sit between them. Restoration adds a detection stage, where a model flags scratches, dust, flicker or missing data, and a repair stage that fills the flagged regions using information from nearby frames. Quality is judged frame by frame and in motion, since a result that looks clean in a still can shimmer or smear when played. Operators tune occlusion handling and artefact thresholds by hand, and most commercial jobs still end with a colourist or restoration artist reviewing the output.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights questions centre on who owns the restored or synthesised frames, on the provenance of the source material, and on whether interpolation alters a work in a way that affects the rights holder or the artist's intent. Restoration of archive film often involves estates, studios and national collections, and the site's count of 92 active intellectual property lawsuits shows how live these disputes are across AI media. Provenance practice means keeping a record of which model version touched which shot, so a finished master can be audited. Nothing here is legal advice, and anyone handling a specific title should take their own advice on clearances and credits.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward fewer manual passes, with restoration and interpolation folded into a single model that handles damage, noise, timing and resolution together. Real time interpolation is already moving into displays and players, which shifts the work from post houses toward the device. Expect more attention to provenance metadata and to consent around deceased performers and archive subjects, and expect the model counts on this site to keep climbing as video generation and restoration converge.
